title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per pair). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10000). The ceiling outcome invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, exact execution accounting, artifact-grounded representative validator traces, quantitative analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, and concrete, artifact-supported prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models requires robust acceptance criteria to prevent harmful, silent, or wrong-but-plausible actions. A practical and increasingly discussed pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration or plan, a deterministic validator mechanically checks correctness and policy constraints, and—when necessary—a repair module synthesizes corrected candidates or triggers human review. Prior system and benchmark work motivate GVR but do not provide standardized, preregistered metrics for validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, or predictive utility for end-to-end guarded success [1]–[5].

We preregistered study AC-2026-03 to measure validator utility in a controlled, paired design that isolates the effect of downstream validator-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each task the generator produced a single initial candidate that was reused by both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator+repair permitted) conditions; therefore any paired difference can only arise from downstream validation/repair. Our primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (H1) expected that a multidimensional validator-metric suite would explain more variance in end-to-end success than a single verifier pass rate. The execution produced a degenerate (ceiling) outcome: every sampled shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator, so baseline and guarded success rates were both 1.0. This paper presents the preregistered design, exact execution accounting, artifact-grounded representative traces, statistical results, diagnostic interpretation of the ceiling, and concrete artifact-supported next-step preregistered arms that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility.
sections.related_work:
Work on GVR-like architectures in code and systems demonstrates how interposing deterministic checks and repair loops can reduce generator-induced stochastic errors and produce auditably accepted outputs; that literature provides both architectural precedent and motivation for applying similar ideas in NetOps [1],[4]. Recent NetOps/AIOps benchmark efforts document realistic failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate verifier insertion to prevent action-triggering errors [2],[3]. Survey and tutorial articles on LLMs and agentic AI for communications and NetOps highlight adaptation and verification trade-offs and argue for evaluating verification cost together with nominal correctness [5].

Importantly, the cited records provide evidence for architectural promise and controlled demonstrations but stop short of delivering a standard validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows that is empirically estimable under preregistered execution semantics. Our study was designed to begin filling that measurement gap with a preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment that isolates validator-triggered repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We interpret prior work conservatively (architectural and motivational) and avoid extrapolating empirical coverage claims beyond what the verified records support.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered design parameters (all archived): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded); task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power plan targeted detecting an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 (α = 0.05, ~80% power under conservative planning assumptions) using n = 200 pairs.

Task generation, constraints, and contamination controls. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at 'very_hard' and 'extreme' difficulty labels. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, a compact intent, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. Contamination and exclusion rules (preregistered) were enforced: exact duplicate-output SHA-256 exclusions, embedding cosine > 0.95 near-duplicate exclusions, and deterministic replacement by next-index. The execution bundle records task_manifest.jsonl and analysis/contamination_summary.csv; no contamination exclusions occurred in this run (contamination_summary empty).

Model and sampling configuration. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini; execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Critically, execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). We explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling behavior may still be nondeterministic. Provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, aligning with exactly one shared initial generation per task.

Validator, scoring rule, and success label. The deterministic validator used is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator emits mechanistic fields per episode: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts when present. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the episode success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call following a validator rejection; repairs and associated provider traces would be recorded and archived when applied.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200. Provider-call audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. All raw responses, per-episode validator traces, provider-call traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle (representative artifact hashes present in the execution manifest).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied in any episode. From analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv: baseline_success_count = 200/200 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0), guarded_success_count = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0), paired contingency n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. The numeric analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and match these reported values.

Representative validator-trace excerpt (artifact-grounded). A compact excerpt from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (verbatim fields):
  pair_id: pair-000004
  normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  parsed_command_count: 4
  required_command_count: 4
  observed_touched_field_count: 3
  valid: true
  repair_applied: false
  validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  validator_version: 5.0

Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode; representative per-episode JSON files are available in execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ within the execution bundle.

Exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN rate estimates are degenerate (no observed false positives or false negatives); detection-latency and repair-invocation distributions are uninformative because repair_applied = false throughout. Missingness_summary.csv shows no missing or failed episodes. Contamination_summary.csv is empty. These facts are artifact-grounded and limit what the confirmatory test can reveal: with baseline success = 1.0 the paired estimator has zero variance and the McNemar test and bootstrap CI are point-mass at 0.00, so the preregistered effect target (10 percentage points) cannot be observed in the present data.
sections.discussion:
Why the ceiling occurred (artifact-grounded diagnosis). Three artifact-supported determinants explain the degenerate outcome: (1) the synthetic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced initial candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic checks for the recorded generation seeds and deterministic task payloads; (2) the preregistered single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 and shared_initial_candidate semantics) removed generator variability as a potential source of disagreement; (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but is not designed to detect subtle semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure yet incorrect-by-intent). The combination of a generator that produced verifier-satisfying candidates and the single-sample design produced a statistical ceiling.

Implications for measurement and design. The paired shared_initial_candidate design is attractive because it isolates downstream repair effects, but it concentrates single-sample ceiling risk when generator and validator align. For studies aimed at estimating validator coverage, artifact-grounded modifications are required: (A) deterministic, preregistered fault-injection in a controlled fraction of tasks to create measurable baseline invalidity; (B) multi-sample stochastic generation per task (initial_generation_calls_per_task ≥ 3) to expose generator variability; and (C) multi-validator comparisons and additional model families to assess external validity across validator and model designs. All three prescriptions are directly supported by the archived adapter semantics and task-manifest replacement rules and can be implemented in a follow-up preregistered execution without manual artifact editing.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate correctly isolates repair effects, but chosen sampling semantics produced the observed ceiling. Construct validity: the binary validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic intent-constraint satisfaction but does not capture semantic intent alignment; this is an intrinsic limitation of mechanistic validators and must be acknowledged for operational interpretation. External validity: the study used a synthetic task bank, a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), and one deterministic validator; hence results do not generalize to production heterogeneity without further multi-validator and multi-model experiments. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance in the primary estimand, so inferential conclusions about validator benefit are not possible from this execution alone. These limitations are recorded in the execution and analysis artifacts and motivate the artifact-grounded follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, recorded generation seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. The execution and analysis artifacts (raw responses, validator traces, provider-call audit, paired contingency tables, bootstrap logs) are archived and reproducible from the supplied bundle. We provide concrete, artifact-supported, preregistered follow-up prescriptions—deterministic fault injection, multi-sample generation, and multi-validator/multi-model comparisons—that are necessary to produce estimable validator FP/FN rates, detection latency distributions, and repair utility in operationally meaningful conditions. The archived artifacts provide the exact inputs and deterministic hooks required to run those follow-ups without ad-hoc manual editing. We publish these artifacts to enable community reanalysis and to serve as the basis for rigorously preregistered next-step experiments that can resolve the open measurement questions outlined here.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could arise only from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling), which increases risk of single-sample ceiling.

Synthetic task bank (difficulty labels 'very_hard'/'extreme') and deterministic task generator do not fully represent heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed in this run; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in the execution manifests.
